title: The hog-grunting trombone, Squeeze Me and Clarence Williams
summary: Hightower explains the trombone hog grunt on the record, says Squeeze Me came from Clarence Williams, and recalls the Chicago bandleader Clarence Jones.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. And that's one of those records that I was telling you where the instruments did the talking. Johnny played on his trombone, this thing was a hog grunting while the band played. Oh, right. See, that's what made the number go, see. And the squeeze me was my, now the squeeze me number, I don't know who that number was. That wasn't my original number. No, it was I think Clarence Williams and Fats Waller.
Yeah, Fats Waller, I think it was Fats Waller.

And some of them got together on it. Clarence Williams or some of them got together. And I got the numbers. And I had been down to the dancing class down there. And what was the piano player's name at the dance that got me the job down there? Clarence Williams.
Clarence Williams. He left him, went to New York to see, you heard of him? Yes, I know him.

You know him personally. Well he's the one that wanted me to record all of this stuff. And he had done, down in Liszt I guess he had somewhere as long about eight or ten numbers that he wanted me to record. Because he said that he'd never heard nobody play them numbers like that. Well you see, when I come in Chicago, I was to go to work for him when he was downtown at Boucher's place, see? Yes. See, but I didn't go down there, see? And when he come out to the Owls Theater, you know he stayed at the Owls Theater a long time. He had a band there too. Clarence Williams? Clarence Jones.
Oh, Clarence Jones. Yeah. Well he went to, you should, Clarence Jones? Clarence Williams, what?
Clarence Williams was in the U.
